initiatives.name: Valterra Platinum Demerger
initiatives.summary: Anglo American completed the demerger of its majority interest in the Platinum Group Metals business, now called Valterra Platinum, in May 2025. The company subsequently sold its remaining 19.9% stake in September 2025 for $2.5 billion.

evidence.title: Successful demerger of PGMs business Valterra Platinum
evidence.summary: Anglo American completed the demerger of its majority interest in the Platinum Group Metals business, now called Valterra Platinum, in May 2025. The company subsequently sold its remaining 19.9% stake in September 2025 for $2.5 billion.
evidence.quote: Following overwhelming approval by shareholders, the demerger took effect on 31 May 2025, with the share consolidation becoming effective on 1 June. On 3 September 2025, we launched an accelerated bookbuild offering of our remaining c.52.2 million ordinary shares of Valterra. The placing of the c.52.2 million ordinary shares raised cash proceeds of ZAR44.1 billion (approximately $2.5 billion).

evidence.title: Valterra Platinum Demerger Completion
evidence.summary: Anglo American completed the demerger of its 51% interest in the PGMs business, Valterra Platinum (formerly Anglo American Platinum), on 31 May 2025. The company also sold its residual 19.9% interest in Valterra Platinum, receiving $2.432 billion in net proceeds.
evidence.quote: on 31 May 2025, Anglo American completed the demerger of its PGMs business, Anglo American Platinum Limited ("Anglo American Platinum") to operate as a stand-alone business known as Valterra Platinum Limited ("Valterra Platinum"). Includes cash received from the sale of our residual 19.9% interest in Valterra Platinum of $2,432 million (net of tax and transaction costs).

initiatives.name: Corporate Transformation Programme
initiatives.summary: Anglo American substantially completed its Corporate and head-office transformation programme in 2025, delivering gross cost savings. This was part of achieving the targeted $1.8 billion cost savings run-rate.

evidence.title: Corporate and head-office transformation programme completion
evidence.summary: Anglo American substantially completed its Corporate and head-office transformation programme in 2025, delivering gross cost savings. This was part of achieving the targeted $1.8 billion cost savings run-rate.
evidence.quote: Driven by gross cost savings of $0.6 billion from the realisation of $0.3 billion run-rate benefits embedded in 2024 including operational and corporate cost savings, as well as a further $0.3 billion from the substantial completion of our Corporate and head-office transformation programme in 2025.

evidence.title: Organizational Structure Deployment
evidence.summary: Anglo American successfully deployed its new organizational structure by end-Q3 2025 and developed the Enterprise Operating Model. The company achieved FY headcount in line with targets and completed employee engagement surveys as part of broader organizational transformation.
evidence.quote: Organisational transformation – Deploy the new organisational structure by end-Q3 (excluding transition roles relating to De Beers), define and deploy the new organisation model and culture by year end, aligned to the simplified portfolio. Organisation structure deployed, with FY headcount in line with target. Enterprise Operating Model developed and deployment in progress.

initiatives.name: Collahuasi Desalination Infrastructure
initiatives.summary: Anglo American reduced total capital expenditure from $3.9 billion in 2024 to $3.3 billion in 2025. The reduction was driven by rephasing of the Venetia underground life-extension at De Beers and planned lower spend at the Woodsmith project.

evidence.title: Collahuasi desalination plant construction
evidence.summary: Anglo American is investing in constructing a desalination plant at Collahuasi joint venture in Chile to supply water requirements when complete in 2026. The company's 44% share of capital spend was $0.3 billion in 2025.
evidence.quote: An example is the ongoing investment in constructing a desalination plant at Collahuasi – our joint venture in Chile. The plant will supply a significant portion of the mine's water requirements when complete in 2026. During 2025, our 44% share of the capital spend was $0.3 billion, with c.$0.1 billion guided for 2026 as the project concludes.

evidence.title: Group Capital Expenditure Reduction
evidence.summary: Anglo American reduced total capital expenditure from $3.9 billion in 2024 to $3.3 billion in 2025. The reduction was driven by rephasing of the Venetia underground life-extension at De Beers and planned lower spend at the Woodsmith project.
evidence.quote: Capital expenditure was $0.6 billion lower compared to the prior year at $3.3 billion (2024: $3.9 billion). Sustaining capital expenditure was lower at $2.7 billion (2024: $2.9 billion), primarily due to rephasing of the Venetia underground life-extension and rationalisation of stay-in- business capex spend at De Beers, and a planned reduction of Collahuasi desalination project spend as it progresses towards completion in 2026.

initiatives.name: Portfolio Held-for-Sale Classification
initiatives.summary: Anglo American classified its Steelmaking Coal and Nickel businesses as held for sale, with assets held for sale totaling $4.6 billion and liabilities of $1.4 billion as of December 2025. The company recognized impairment losses of $464 million for Steelmaking Coal and $104 million for Nickel businesses.

evidence.title: Assets Held for Sale Classification
evidence.summary: Anglo American classified its Steelmaking Coal and Nickel businesses as held for sale, with assets held for sale totaling $4.6 billion and liabilities of $1.4 billion as of December 2025. The company recognized impairment losses of $464 million for Steelmaking Coal and $104 million for Nickel businesses.
evidence.quote: Management has determined that the Steelmaking Coal and Nickel businesses each met the criteria to be presented as held for sale at 31 December 2025. As such, the Group has presented assets held for sale of $4,590 million (2024: $2,530 million) and liabilities of $1,413 million (2024: $363 million) as at 31 December 2025. Management has recognised an impairment loss of $464 million and $104 million in relation to the Steelmaking Coal and Nickel businesses, respectively, as at 31 December 2025.

initiatives.name: AI Centre of Excellence and Predictive Maintenance
initiatives.summary: Anglo American established an AI Centre of Excellence and deployed AI predictive maintenance tools across 200+ assets, saving approximately 1,000 hours of downtime. The company is also implementing Assisted Core Logging technology that reduces lithology log creation time by 90%.

evidence.title: AI Centre of Excellence and predictive maintenance deployment
evidence.summary: Anglo American established an AI Centre of Excellence and deployed AI predictive maintenance tools across 200+ assets, saving approximately 1,000 hours of downtime. The company is also implementing Assisted Core Logging technology that reduces lithology log creation time by 90%.
evidence.quote: That is why we have established the AI Centre of Excellence and Information Management to provide clear governance, AI risk management and learning programmes, to ultimately ensure our use of AI is responsible and value-accretive across the whole of our business. For example, we have leveraged predictive maintenance technology to monitor over 200 assets across our sites (on a simplified portfolio basis), enabling earlier warning of equipment deterioration, making planned interventions possible and also saving approximately 1,000 hours of downtime across our sites as at the end of 2025.

evidence.title: Kumba UHDMS Project Investment

initiatives.name: Anglo Teck Merger Formation
initiatives.summary: Anglo American announced a merger of equals with Teck Resources to form Anglo Teck, a global critical minerals powerhouse. The merger received overwhelming shareholder approval in December 2025 and regulatory approval from the Government of Canada.
initiatives.investmentSummary: $1.4 billion of annual underlying EBITDA uplift

evidence.title: Merger with Teck Resources to form Anglo Teck
evidence.summary: Anglo American announced a merger of equals with Teck Resources to form Anglo Teck, a global critical minerals powerhouse. The merger received overwhelming shareholder approval in December 2025 and regulatory approval from the Government of Canada.
evidence.quote: In September 2025, we announced our merger of equals with Teck to form a global critical minerals powerhouse, Anglo Teck, unlocking significant value both in the near and long term, and offering investors more than 70% exposure to copper. We expect to realise $800 million in pre-tax recurring annual synergies and an additional $1.4 billion of annual underlying EBITDA uplift through the adjacency of Collahuasi with Teck's Quebrada Blanca operation, to potentially establish one of the largest copper complexes in the world.

initiatives.name: Sakatti Critical Minerals Project
initiatives.summary: Anglo American's Sakatti project in Finland was awarded 'Strategic Project' status by the European Commission in March 2025 under the Critical Raw Materials Act, benefiting from more efficient permitting processes.

evidence.title: Sakatti awarded EU Strategic Project status
evidence.summary: Anglo American's Sakatti project in Finland was awarded 'Strategic Project' status by the European Commission in March 2025 under the Critical Raw Materials Act, benefiting from more efficient permitting processes.
evidence.quote: On 25 March 2025, Sakatti was awarded 'Strategic Project' status by the European Commission. Under the CRMA, Strategic Projects are considered to be in the public interest due to their importance in ensuring security of supply of strategic raw materials in the EU, thereby benefiting from more efficient processing of permitting applications and therefore more predictable development timelines.

initiatives.name: Carbon Neutrality Target Reset
initiatives.summary: Anglo American redefined its climate ambition with a 30% reduction target in GHG emissions by 2030 and carbon neutrality by 2040 for its simplified portfolio, excluding Kumba Iron Ore. The Board approved these revised targets in 2025.

evidence.title: Updated carbon neutrality targets for simplified portfolio
evidence.summary: Anglo American redefined its climate ambition with a 30% reduction target in GHG emissions by 2030 and carbon neutrality by 2040 for its simplified portfolio, excluding Kumba Iron Ore. The Board approved these revised targets in 2025.
evidence.quote: Our revised ambition and targets, aligned with our Sustainability Strategy and which apply to our simplified portfolio, were approved by the Board during 2025. For our 2030 Scope 1 and 2 target, which covers the whole simplified portfolio, we are conscious of the importance of maintaining a high degree of confidence in our ability to deliver the decarbonisation required, whilst we grow our production of future-enabling metals and minerals.
